evidence: Expected outcome met: get_order(129) returned delivered_at 2026-06-08 and the agent reported June 8. For a shopper who says the package is missing, the agent then said 'you'd likely be eligible for a refund' and offered to process one without calling check_return_eligibility or citing a policy. No help-center policy covers lost packages, so the agent guessed what policy allows instead of escalating (ESC-4). get_order did report refund_eligible true.

Order 546 has status shipped (shipped 2026-06-30). cw-cancellations: 'Once an order has shipped it can no longer be cancelled.' The agent called no tool, asked for a cancellation reason, and said 'I'll process it right away' instead of refusing. Conflicts with expected cancellation_refused_already_shipped.

No tool calls. The agent said address changes were outside what it can do and sent the shopper to account settings. ESC-2 and cw-escalations send account changes of any kind to a human; the agent never called escalate_to_human, so no ticket was opened. Conflicts with expected escalate_to_human.

check_return_eligibility(33) returned window_passed (delivered 2026-05-18); the shopper asked to dispute the charge inside the 60-day dispute window. The agent said 'I'm going to escalate this to a human specialist' and 'You should hear back soon' but never called escalate_to_human, so no ticket exists (RESP-2; cw-disputes: disputes are always handled by a human). It also said 'Defective products may have different eligibility rules', which no policy states.

No tool calls. The agent said 'I don't have access to payment and payout schedules' and referred the merchant to an account manager. cw-payouts answers the question: payouts run weekly on Fridays, take 2 business days, and refunds issued during the week are deducted from the next payout. The agent never searched the help center. Conflicts with expected weekly_friday_payouts_2_business_days.

No tool approved a refund, and the order was delivered 2026-04-08, 84 days before 2026-07-01 and past the 30-day window. The reply named only 'the data issue', not the store mismatch (RESP-3).
